challengesData.heading:
Boardroom AV Failures & 
 How We Design Them Out
challengesData.subhead: Most boardroom AV failures stem from misinterpreted room acoustics and delayed design choices. Early surveys and tests prevent operational friction before installation.

problem.title: Remote directors can't hear the room
problem.text: Reflective room surfaces cause heavy echo, preventing remote directors from following the conversation.

solution.title: Acoustics-driven equipment selection
solution.text: We test room acoustics, steer microphone pickup to seats, and tune DSP echo filters to your room's measured decay.

problem.title: Meetings start ten minutes late
problem.text: Scattered remotes, wrong display leads, and complex meeting joins waste valuable time before every call.
problem.tagline: Delayed calls and frequent IT intervention

solution.title: One touch panel. One button to join.
solution.text: Our engineers program a single interface for audio, display, camera and lighting, then test it before sign-off.
solution.tagline: Meetings start on time without IT assistance

problem.title: The far end of the table can't read the screen
problem.text: Catalog display sizes ignore room depth, making spreadsheets unreadable past the middle of the table.
problem.tagline: Forced to rely on paper handouts

solution.title: Display sized to your farthest seat
solution.text: We size the display from your viewing distance and move to an LED wall when the table is too long for any panel.

problem.title: Confidential discussions leave the room
problem.text: Private discussions drift into hallways while shared guest Wi-Fi exposes sensitive board data.

solution.title: Speech privacy and a secured network
solution.text: Exterior acoustic masking protects board privacy, and encrypted calls run on a dedicated network segment.

problem.title: Finger-pointing leaves room faults unresolved
problem.text: When calls drop, AV installers blame networks, and the IT team points back. Neither group owns the faults.
problem.tagline: Faults that stay open for days

solution.title: One team owns AV and the network
solution.text: GS IT handles both AV and the underlying networks, so there is one number to call and one team accountable.

problem.title: Cables and hardware clutter the board table
problem.text: Loose cables, adapters and visible hardware clutter the table and spoil the finish.

solution.title: Hardware hidden, sharing made wireless
solution.text: Cables run through floor boxes and joinery, equipment sits in ceiling voids, and wireless sharing removes laptop leads.

faqHeaderData.heading:
Common Questions on 
 Boardroom AV Solutions

faqData.question: How long does a boardroom AV project take?
faqData.answer: The timeline depends on room size, equipment lead times and how quickly the design drawings are approved. Survey and design come first, followed by procurement, installation, commissioning, testing and handover. We share a project schedule once the design is approved and the equipment is ordered. If your space needs acoustic panels, they should be installed before the AV work begins.

faqData.question: Can existing equipment be reused when upgrading a boardroom?
faqData.answer: Yes, existing equipment can be reused if it matches your new layout and performance needs. Functional displays and speakers often integrate well into an updated boardroom system. However, older video codecs and video bars rarely carry over due to evolving Zoom and Teams software requirements. A pre-project survey identifies reusable gear.

faqData.question: How many microphones does a sixteen-seat boardroom need?
faqData.answer: A sixteen-seat table is usually covered by two tabletop microphones placed along its center, so every seat sits close to one. If the table must stay clear, a single ceiling array can cover it instead, as large-format units reach up to about 9 m × 9 m. A second array or extra table mics is only necessary for ceilings well above 3 meters or when specific seats require dedicated audio priority.

faqData.question: What display size suits a boardroom table of six meters?
faqData.answer: A 98-inch panel works well for standard presentation slides, staying legible up to about 7.3 meters. However, detailed spreadsheets on the same panel stay readable only to about 4.9 meters, well short of the far end of a six-meter table. For dense data at that length, a second display, a 136-inch LED wall or seat-level monitors bring content closer to the far end.

faqData.question: Does a boardroom need a DSP when the video bar already handles audio?
faqData.answer: Not in smaller boardrooms, as a video bar handles audio well up to around twelve seats. For a larger boardroom conference system where front-mounted mics lose clarity, we pair ceiling or tabletop microphones with a dedicated DSP to keep every voice clear.

faqData.question: Should acoustic treatment be finished before the AV installation?
faqData.answer: Acoustic work must wrap up before AV installation begins. Wall panels and sound baffling alter room reverberation, directly impacting how microphone gain and processing are calibrated. Installing panels afterward means re-tuning the system and extending project timelines.

faqData.question: How is confidential audio kept from leaving the boardroom?
faqData.answer: We study your room dimensions and physical build to design an integrated boardroom AV system that minimizes sound leakage. Acoustic masking emitters outside the room obscure residual speech bleed. We provide the best boardroom video conferencing solutions with calls running on a dedicated network segment, kept apart from guest Wi-Fi and managed under your existing IT security policies.

faqData.question: Can we try the equipment before it is ordered?
faqData.answer: Yes. Once the design drawings are approved, a product demo lets your team see and hear the shortlisted microphones, cameras, and displays working side by side, and try the touch panel and one-touch join. Final equipment choices are confirmed only after that session, so the order is based on what your team experienced firsthand.

faqData.question: Do the AI features in a boardroom need extra licensing?
faqData.answer: On-device processing like active speaker tracking and background noise suppression comes built into the hardware. Higher-level features like automated meeting transcripts and action item generation run on your video platform, depending entirely on the license tier your organization maintains.

faqData.question: Who supports the room after handover?
faqData.answer: Your internal IT staff manage day-to-day operations using the training and documentation provided at handover. For ongoing maintenance, an optional AV AMC agreement adds quick remote troubleshooting, scheduled preventive visits, and SLA-backed response times.
